expectations.text: B1: Flags z.any() and replaces it with a safer type (z.unknown / branded / proper primitive)
expectations.evidence: Problem #1 flags `id: z.any()` as CRITICAL; corrected code uses `id: z.string().uuid()` and advises z.unknown() only when shape is genuinely unknown.

expectations.text: B2: Flags the missing email validation and adds .email()
expectations.evidence: Problem #2 'email: z.string() — no format validation'; corrected `email: z.string().email()`.

expectations.text: B3: Flags age typed as string and coerces/uses a number so schema matches the intended type
expectations.evidence: Problem #3 flags string/number drift; corrected `age: z.number().int().positive()` plus explicit z.coerce.number() guidance for form input.

expectations.text: B4: Flags role as a plain string and switches to z.enum
expectations.evidence: Problem #4 flags `role: z.string()`; corrected uses `export const UserRole = z.enum([...])` referenced as `role: UserRole`.

expectations.text: B5: Replaces the hand-written `User` type with z.infer<typeof UserSchema>
expectations.evidence: Problem #5 says delete the duplicate type; corrected `export type User = z.infer<typeof UserSchema>`.

expectations.text: B6: Recommends safeParse (+ error handling) over parse for the untrusted `body: unknown`
expectations.evidence: Problem #6 flags `.parse()` on unknown; corrected handler uses `UserSchema.safeParse(body)` and branches, returning `error.flatten().fieldErrors`.

expectations.text: B7: Provides corrected, coherent code implementing the fixes
expectations.evidence: Complete corrected block with enum, uuid, coerce note, inferred type, and safeParse handler with a discriminated SignupResult; Zod-3-idiomatic (z.string().uuid()/.email()), consistent with the pinned version.

eval_feedback.overall: All 7 satisfied. Corrected code uses Zod-3 method-form APIs (z.string().uuid()/.email(), flatten()), which matches the repo's pinned v3.24; no assertion tests version-correctness, so this advantage is invisible to the score.
